name: Extraneural Perineurioma

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Histopathological and Immunohistochemical Diagnostic Criteria for Extraneural Perineurioma

criteria.description: Presence of spindle cells arranged in whorled or storiform patterns with elongated nuclei
Positive immunoreactivity for epithelial membrane antigen (EMA) and claudin-1, with negative S-100 protein staining
Slow-growing, painless, well-circumscribed soft tissue mass typically located in the subcutaneous tissue or deep soft tissues
MRI showing a well-defined, homogeneous mass without infiltration of adjacent structures

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Histopathological confirmation with characteristic spindle cell morphology and positive EMA immunostaining, along with clinical presentation of a slow-growing soft tissue mass
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis requires exclusion of other peripheral nerve sheath tumors such as schwannoma and neurofibroma.

searchTerms: slow growing painless lump under skin

pathognomonic.symptomName: Well-circumscribed soft tissue tumor on palpation
searchTerms: smooth edged tumor felt on skin

common.symptomName: Localized swelling at the tumor site
Occasional numbness or paresthesia due to nerve compression
searchTerms: intermittent tingling due to nerve compression

occasional.symptomName: Motor weakness distal to the lesion
searchTerms: loss of strength distal to mass

occasional.symptomName: Mild local erythema overlying the mass
Intermittent cramping or discomfort near the tumor
Limited range of motion if lesion is near a joint
searchTerms: reduced range of motion by lesion

rare.notes: May suggest malignant transformation or alternative diagnosis

imaging: MRI demonstrating well-circumscribed, homogeneous soft tissue mass without infiltration
Ultrasound showing hypoechoic lesion with well-defined margins
genetic: Occasional deletions or mutations involving chromosome 22q (NF2 gene region) reported in some cases
other: Histopathology showing spindle cells with elongated nuclei arranged in whorls
Immunohistochemistry positive for EMA and claudin-1, negative for S-100 protein

distinguishingFeatures: Strong S-100 protein positivity on immunohistochemistry
Antoni A and Antoni B histological patterns
Mixed cellular composition including Schwann cells, fibroblasts, and perineurial cells
High mitotic activity and necrosis on histology

redFlags: Ulceration or skin breakdown over lesion
references: Weiss SW, Goldblum JR. Enzinger and Weiss's Soft Tissue Tumors. 6th ed. Elsevier; 2014.
Hornick JL, Fletcher CDM. Soft tissue perineurioma: clinicopathologic analysis of 81 cases. Am J Surg Pathol. 2005;29(7):845-858.
